sentences.text: Revenue compounded 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201].
The path was cyclical rather than smooth: revenue fell 22.4% in FY2020 to $41.7 billion [F5][D198] and then rose 22.1% in FY2021 [F6][D251].
The FY2020 decline came from lower sales volume driven by lower end-user demand and dealer inventory changes across all three primary segments [P59].
FY2023 was the margin peak, with operating profit up 64.0% to $13.0 billion on favorable price realization and higher sales volume [F18][D358][P31].
FY2025 revenue rose 4.3% to $67.6 billion on higher sales volume, partly offset by unfavorable price realization [F10][D463][P13].
North America supplied 54.2% of FY2025 revenue and 3.4pp of its 4.3% growth [D513][D515][D463].
North America sales rose 6% on higher sales volume, mainly higher sales of equipment to end users [P12].
Power & Energy grew 11.6% and contributed 5.2pp, while Construction Industries fell 1.6% and subtracted 0.6pp [D758][D759][D765][D766].
Construction Industries' decline was primarily unfavorable price realization of $1.136 billion, partly offset by higher sales volume [P8].
Operating income fell 14.7% against 4.3% revenue growth, so incremental operating margin was -69.1% [F20][D464][D463][D488].
FY2025 operating margin of 16.5% sits above the 14.3% window median but below the 20.2% FY2024 high [F30][D1123][D1122].
The margin fell 3.7pp, with cost of revenue subtracting 4.2pp and SG&A and R&D roughly neutral [D476][D490][D491][D492].

Operating profit fell $1.921 billion primarily on unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion and unfavorable price realization of $817 million, with manufacturing costs largely reflecting higher tariffs [P9].
Net margin of 13.1% trailed operating margin by 3.4pp, with a 24.0% effective tax rate and $892 million of other income [F50][F30][D1168][D449][X110].
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion was 1.32x net income, above the 1.16x window median [F80][F40][D450][D1158].
Free cash flow fell 11.2% to $8.9 billion, a 13.2% margin against a 11.9% median [F100][D469][D447][D1129].
Capex rose 41.9% to $2.8 billion, 4.2% of revenue and 1.25x D&A, the highest ratio in the window [F90][D470][D446][D452].
Machinery, Power & Energy operating cash flow rose to $12.278 billion on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes paid [P4].
Cash rose 44.9% to $9.98 billion while total debt grew 14.1% to $36.2 billion, leaving net debt of $26.2 billion [F140][D472][D455][D485][D456].
That net debt equals 38.8% of revenue, a smaller net debt burden than the peer median of 59.4% of revenue, ranking 67th percentile of three peers [D457][D1170][D1169].
These totals omit long-term debt due within one year, which the filer reports at $7.1 billion in FY2025 [R7][X180].
Buybacks of $5.19 billion plus dividends of $2.75 billion were 89.0% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 3.5% [X140][X150][D459][D483].
Total debt and net cash omit long-term debt due within one year, reported at $7.1 billion in FY2025, so leverage is understated every year [R7][X180].
Net debt rose for a second year, from $22.1 billion in FY2023 to $26.2 billion in FY2025, on the same incomplete debt base [R1][D350][D456].
FY2021-FY2025 net income in the table is proxy-sourced and differs from the 10-K by up to 0.06%, so the 10-K figures are used where precision matters [R3][F40][X20].
Revenue fell 3.4% in FY2024 on lower sales volume, partly offset by favorable price realization [R2][F9][D410][P22].
Operating margin: a FY2026 reading below the 14.3% window median would confirm the FY2025 erosion, while a return above 20.2% would reverse it [D1123][D1122].
Capex: a ratio to D&A above the FY2025 1.25x would extend the capital-intensity build and pressure free cash flow [D452].
Tariff-driven manufacturing costs: management guides first-quarter 2026 profit to be squeezed by higher manufacturing costs in Construction and Resource Industries [P14].
